title.narrative: Guyana Petroleum Resources Governance and Management Project

description.narrative: The objective of the Petroleum Resources Governance and Management Project is to support the enhancement of legal and institutional frameworks and the strengthening of the capacity of key institutions to manage the oil and gas sector in Guyana. There are four components to the project, the first component being enhancement of legal framework and stakeholder engagement. This component aims to support the update of Guyana's legal and regulatory frameworks for the governance and oversight of the O and G sector as well as support stakeholder engagement and transparency. This component includes two subcomponents: update the legal and regulatory frameworks for the O and G sector, and support stakeholder engagement and transparency. The second component is the capacity building of key institutions. This component includes four subcomponents: support immediate technical needs at key institutions with responsibility for O and G, support critical training needs at key institutions with responsibility for O and G, build up petroleum data management, and strengthen environmental and social management. The third component is the enhancement of fiscal management. Finally, the fourth component is the project management. This component will provide support to the government of the co-operative Republic of Guyana to manage and coordinate all project activities financed under the project. More specifically, it will provide support and build the Government's procurement, financial management, safeguards management, monitoring and evaluation capacity through the provision to the Project Implementing Unit (PIU), Department of Energy, of technical advisory services, training, recruitment of instrumental staff as needed, acquisition of goods, and operating costs.

The project development objective is to support the enhancement of legal and institutional frameworks and the strengthening of the capacity of key institutions to manage the oil and gas sector in Guyana.

condition.narrative: Schedule 2, Section B.1. The Government, through the MOTP, shall carry out the Project in accordance with the provisions of amanual (the “Project Operations Manual”) acceptable to IDA.

Schedule 2, Section C.1.(b) The Government, through the MOTP, shall ensure that for the purposes of implementing Part B.4(a) ofthe Project: (A) the SESA is prepared, consulted, disclosed and adopted in accordance with the SESA TORs; and (B) therecommendations of the SESA are applied during Project implementation, as applicable, all in a manner acceptable to IDA.

Schedule 2, Section C.2 The Government, through the MOTP, shall ensure that: (a) all consultancies related to technicalassistance, design and capacity building under the Project, the application of whose results could have environmental, social andhealth and safety implications, as determined by IDA, shall only be undertaken pursuant to terms of reference reviewed and foundsatisfactory by IDA; and (b) such terms of reference shall require the technical assistance, design and capacity buildingactivities to take into account the requirements of the applicable Safeguards Policies and EHS Guidelines, and to be based on GIIP.

Schedule 2, Section I.A. The Government, through the MOTP, shall operate and maintain throughout Project implementation, aProject Implementation Unit (the “PIU”) with staff, functions and responsibilities acceptable to IDA, and as set forth in theProject Operations Manual.

title.narrative: Communications strategy on O&G sector issues implemented

comment.narrative:
As of June 2025, this indicator measuring the number of annual Communications Strategy Implementation Reports has not been met. No such implementation reports were produced.
However, the Ministry of Natural Resources developed a Communications Strategic Plan in December 2016, with assistance from the IDB.
Later, a Communications and Knowledge Management Strategy for 2022 - 2026 was developed by the Ministry. The Strategy examined the gaps from the earlier Communications Strategy and presented measures to address them.
GPRGMP funded a Consultancy for Strategic Communications Support to the Department of Energy (2019) and a Consultancy for Website Development (2019), both of which assisted in addressing communication and stakeholder engagement gaps identified previously. Their recommendations were reflected in a number of sector reports published between 2021 and 2023.

title.narrative: Stakeholder consultations conducted on new legislation/regulations for O&G sector

comment.narrative:
This indicator monitors the organization of consultations with relevant stakeholders on key pieces of legislation/regulations for the oil and gas sector, drafted with the support of the project.
As of October 2024, this indicator target had been met.
Stakeholders consultations took place with project support in August 2019 to assess the needs and scope for new sector legislation and regulations. Four stakeholder consultations were held during development of the Local Content Act in 2021. Draft Petroleum Activities Act, Model Petroleum Agreements for Deep Water and Shallow Water, and a Gas Monetization Strategy were subject to public consultations in 2023.
